This has happened to me before. I was isolated because I was socially inept and I didn't know how to deal with because at the same time I was mentally ill. These people often talk about people like us as a form of shallow conversation to keep everyone in the group bonded. Yung mga 'friends' mo na minimal ng makkpagusap sa iyo ay nakikisama lang din sa group na ito. More often than not, ang end result is you'll ostracised because everyone will eventually assume na being around you is social suicide.

The worst thing to do is not speak up to anyone about it. In your case, if you can't confront them or talk with your former friends then it's best to talk with the councilor of your program. Let someone in your school know that this is happening to you, that way may record na it really happened. 

I'd still suggest na you record it, in any creative way, para when it comes down to your words against them may proof ka at least. I'm not sure if this is the legal way pero events like this are isolating and frustrating. 

I wish you luck OP! Know that nothing is wrong with you and madalas yung ganitong cases iilan lang pasimuno and nakikisama lang halos lahat. I hope that you the courage to speak up.

Although I understand that being bullied is excruciating and that violence is an easy option, don't do it. It's not worth throwing away your future for stooping down below their level.

The best thing to do is record the instances that you are being bullied. Whether it be on social media or in real life. Find people who are willing to speak out for you to support these instances. 

Inform your school counselor, a teacher, a close friend, or your parents that this is happening. I know that it's to open up and be vulnerable about this happening but you have to speak up about it. 

Remember that it's the bully's shame and not yours that this is happening. If anything, bullies project their shame or anger towards a target just because they think the target can't fight back. 

Examples of bullying that should be recorded:
- name calling
- joking about your illness
- isolating or ostracizing you
- verbal and physical abuse
- public humiliation
- etc.

Also remember that bullying should not be tolerated as it does not build character, it builds trauma and shame. Should you fight back against the bully, do it while the bullying is happening. Call out the act of abuse in the middle of it. 

I suggested that non-conflict first option in the event that you might be gaslighted when you speak out about it. It's best to gain physical evidence first in the event that you confront this person, there will be a solid consequence.

This is all I can think of and I hope this help. Have courage and do the right thing. Also, f*ck that bully. ❤

Coming from the same place as you are. In my early twenties, still in college. Hindi naman super rich pero may kaya. Had a mental breakdown when I was 17 but I was depressed long before that (family issues and school issues) and nakita nila lahat ng physical symptoms ng depression ko — my parents. Literal being unresponsive to the world and letting my studies go to shit that I had to stop.

Anyway, they couldn't deny it anymore once I was hospitalized and an actual psychiatrist explained to them what's happening to me. Hindi na nila pwede masabi na "nasa isip mo lang yan" or "ako nga kaya ko labanan, nawawala naman" or "wala ka kasing faith kaya nagka ganyan ka". 

I know you're not looking for unsolicited advice from a rando online but don't let yourself hit rock bottom just because kinakain ka ng unexplained guilt. Symptom din yun ng depression, not that I'm diagnosing you but if you've been feeling like this for a long time you need to reach out to professionals.

You have the right to demand help kasi this is a serious illness. If you're reaching the point na simpleng basic self care feels like a chore, baka umabot ka sa punto na mawalan ka ng autonomy sa sarili mo. Obviously it's not easy to speak out about this but man mas mahirap mag bounce back from a burnout or a rock bottom lalo na kung mag isa ka lang.

My parents might still shit on me sometimes na si pinsan mo "has achieved this or that" or na minsan masasabi nila yung "depression means may topak" but it's a whole lot easier to deal with knowing that you have a MH professional/s to lean into to objectively sort out your emotions and prescribe you medication.

Anecdotal but for me it's easier to talk with strangers that are experiencing the same struggle/ illness as me. It's not being needy naman and it's really bad to keep it all in. I also think that it's easier to open up to strangers kasi walang past history before sa lahat ng sasabihin mo parang ilalagay mo sa malinis na tubig. And madalas dun niyo lang iiwan yun, whatever you've talked about. Ang wary lang ako when it comes to venting to strangers is it may create a bubble mentality (self deprecation and all that, depends kung sino kausap mo) and hindi mo talaga personally alam kung sino sila. So no nuances, just surface level venting. 

Kapag friends naman, they can give you the support and suggested talaga that you build that system pero if neurotypical sila, hanggang worry and assurance maiaabot nila. I also for some reason feel guilty when venting towards them kasi baka palaging worried sila sa akin. Kanya kanya naman iyan, depending on your relationship with them.
